body.text: Overview and Empirical Foundations of Deep learning
What separates informed decisions about Deep learning from costly guesswork in technology? Primary context, measurable criteria, and disciplined execution form the foundation of lasting value.
Every leap in modern computing traces back to breakthroughs like Deep learning. Look past the hype and you find concrete engineering trade-offs in speed, energy efficiency, and system architecture.

In machine learning, deep learning (DL) focuses on utilizing multilayered neural networks to perform tasks such as classification, regression, and representation learning. The field takes inspiration from biological neuroscience and revolves around stacking artificial neurons into layers and "training" them to process data.
The adjective "deep" refers to the use of multiple layers (ranging from three to several hundred or thousands) in the network. Methods used can be supervised, semi-supervised or unsupervised.

Some common deep learning network architectures include fully connected networks, deep belief networks, recurrent neural networks, convolutional neural networks, generative adversarial networks, transformers, and neural radiance fields.

These architectures have been applied to fields including computer vision, speech recognition, natural language processing, machine translation, bioinformatics, drug design, medical image analysis, climate science, material inspection and board game programs, where they have produced results comparable to and in some cases surpassing human expert performance.
